Items.Authors: Nico Van der Merwe, Lisa Crause, Eben Wiid, Francois Strumpfer, John A. Booth, Willem Van Der Westhuizen, Michael Sam, Nicolaas Jacobs, Denville Gibbons, Johan Hendricks
Items.Title: Restoring adjustment range in the SALT primary mirror
Items.Abstract: During the 2025 SALT shutdown, a major task was recovering global tip/tilt and piston adjustment of the segmented primary mirror. Several segments had reached the limits of their coarse actuators, with some close to the truss and others too far from it. A systematic procedure was developed to regain travel by making small, controlled adjustments to the coarse actuators while compensating with larger fine-actuator changes, keeping all segments within CCAS capture range. This allowed daytime mechanical work to be paired with nighttime CCAS-guided alignment without de-focusing the array. In total, 40 iterations were completed, restoring roughly 4 mm of usable travel to the most constrained segments.

Items.Authors: Ryan D. Hersey, Max Millar-Blanchaer, Skyler Palatnick, Jaren Ashcraft, Daniel Shanks, James K. Wallace, Tobias Wenger, Sarah Choi, Courtney Duong
Items.Title: Results from early prototyping of a metasurface polarization aberration corrector (PAC) for large observatories
Items.Abstract: Polarization aberrations pose a unique challenge for high contrast imaging as they cannot be corrected by traditional adaptive optics systems. They manifest as speckles in the imaging plane, masking as exoplanets. We present the simulated performance and in-lab characterization of a metasurface device for correcting the polarization aberrations generated by the mirrors of large telescopes.

Items.Authors: Jeffrey A. De Lucca, Alexandra N. Higley, Bridget C. O'Meara, Randall L. McEntaffer, Nathaniel Hamme, Ross C. McCurdy, James H. Tutt, Cooper B. Akers, Garrett A. Brady, Suraj P. Chandran, Ivonne Ferrera, Aditi M. Gangadharan, Jake A. McCoy, Nolan McPhaul, Lily McEntaffer, Natasha Patel, Tristen M. Sextro, Cora Tebbe, Zoey Tran, Joshua Wang, Vadim Burwitz, Gisela D. Hartner, Andreas Langmeier, Thomas G. Müller, Surangkhana Rukdee, Thomas Schmidt, David Colebrook, David Gopinath, Andrew D. Holland, Karen Holland, Daniel Evan, Stefano Basso, Alberto Moretti, Daniele Spiga, Casey T. DeRoo
Items.Title: Reverse telescope illumination of JET-X
Items.Abstract: To support the Pathfinder Off-Plane Grating Rocket Experiment (OGRE-P) suborbital rocket mission, the Joint European Telescope for X-ray Astronomy (JET-X) optic must be fully illuminated under laboratory conditions. We demonstrate a cost-effective alignment method using optical light and a hobbyist Dobsonian telescope operated in reverse to generate a large-diameter collimated beam. This approach minimizes expense while achieving the necessary illumination for calibration. We present technical details of the instrumentation setup and alignment procedure to enable other researchers to replicate this low-cost technique for similar large-aperture optical systems.

Items.Authors: Priscila Pires, Victor Echeverria, Francisco Gajardo
Items.Title: Review of the stripping process for aluminum coating in NOIRLab
Items.Abstract: This work, conducted by AURA/NOIRLab and La Serena University, investigates how to optimize the chemical stripping process used to remove aluminum coatings from the Blanco 4-m and SOAR telescope mirrors. Although high-quality coatings are essential for optical performance, current stripping methods have changed little over time and lack clarity regarding efficiency and reaction mechanisms. The study followed three stages: reproducing existing procedures, testing controlled variations in concentration and application methods, and evaluating acidic, basic, and redox solutions through visual inspection and conductivity measurements. Results show that a single well-formulated acidic or basic solution can fully remove aluminum, eliminating the traditional multi-step sequence. The next steps are to apply these results to telescope mirrors and quantify gains in time, chemical use, safety, and waste reduction.

Items.Authors: Nicolas Blind, Bruno Chazelas, Muskan Shinde, Isaac Dinis, Nathanaël Restori, Bachar Wehbe, Leonie Hoerner, Christophe Lovis, Mary Angelie M. Alagao, Romain Fétick, Vincent Chambouleyron, Cédric Taïssir Héritier Salama, Benoît Neichel, Jean-François Sauvage, Thierry Fusco, Sylvain Cetre
Items.Title: RISTRETTO front-end: entering the PDR phase
Items.Abstract: RISTRETTO is a diffraction-limited visible instrument using high-dispersion coronagraphy to detect and characterize nearby rocky exoplanets such as Proxima Centauri b. Its Front-End enables high-contrast single-mode fiber injection at 2 λ/D and includes an XAO system, a coronagraphic IFU based on the new PIAAN concept, and a high-precision closed-loop ADC. Recent milestones include the laboratory demonstration of PIAAN, on-sky validation of the NIR unmodulated pyramid WFS, and deployment of the DD4AO real-time controller. These results support consolidated XAO simulations, a complete error budget, and the tolerance analyses needed to launch detailed Front-End design. We present these developments and report the outcomes of the System Architecture Review ahead of the PDR phase.

Items.Authors: Nathanaël Restori, Nicolas Blind, Bruno Chazelas, Christophe Lovis, Christoph Mordasini, Muskan Shinde
Items.Title: RISTRETTO: two-photon polymerization (2PP) 3D printing and glass laser micro-fabrication for singlemode integral field units (IFUs)
Items.Abstract: RISTRETTO is a diffraction-limited instrument for detecting the reflected light from exoplanets in the visible. One of its core components is a seven-spaxels IFU made of single mode fibers. Due to their small core size, the alignment tolerances between fibers and micro-lens are extremely tight, on the order of a few hundreds of nanometers. This ensures efficiency and proper sky coverage. The coupling efficiency requirement for RISTRETTO is xx% [Blind et al. same conference]. This is the design driver. These tolerances are difficult to acheive using traditional techniques. We present the results of our prototyping activities, showing the performances obtained using Two-Photon Polymerization (2PP) 3D printing and glass laser micro-fabrication.

Items.Authors: Logan Pawlowski, Nicolas Hernandez, Amit Ashok
Items.Title: Robust and Compact Origami Pyramid Wavefront Sensor Design for Small Telescopes
Items.Abstract: Here, we present a compact, robust, and unmodulated PyWFS architecture. We combine an economical double-roof-prism configuration with a geometrically optimized folded ”origami” relay that reduces the physical package length by  about 74% relative to the unfolded configuration, and a custom machined structure fixes the optimized  mirror positions and separations, reducing alignment degrees of freedom and improving mechanical stability. A  neural network (NN) based non-linear wavefront reconstruction eliminates high-speed mechanical modulation  required by linearized interaction-matrix (IM) reconstruction, thereby also extending the sensor’s operating  range, and a laboratory validation of wavefront reconstruction is performed with multiple atmospheric scenes. The proposed unmodulated PyWFS optical design coupled with an NN-based reconstruction approach provides a practical pathway toward compact PyWFS deployment on small-aperture telescopes.

Items.Authors: Greg Jolley, Annino Vaccarella, Marc White, Alexey Grigoriev, Hana Benhizia, Joice Mathew, Nian Jiang, Michael Ellis, Warrick Schofield, Mark Downing, Rob Sharp
Items.Title: Rosella: the compact detector controller for small satellite science missions
Items.Abstract: Rosella delivers the full programmability and performance of traditional large-observatory controllers in a compact, modular, power optimised and radiation-tolerant architecture for space applications. It provides high-speed, low-noise readout of advanced detectors - including Leonardo SAPHIRA eAPD arrays and Teledyne HxRG focal plane arrays - making it a potential detector control solution for small-satellite science missions and future missions like Gaia-NIR. Rosella supports up to 32 video channels with an analog pixel data resolution of 16-bits. Low-noise detector power and bias supplies are provided by a voltage programmable sequencing circuit allowing for control over voltage dependent detector characteristics including avalanche gain. Strategies to enhance tolerance to radiation are discussed. Rosella’s performance characteristic testing results of an engineering model controlling a Leonardo Saphira detector at cryogenic temperatures will be presented.

Items.Authors: Maud P. Langlois, clementine bechet, Laura Schreiber, Michel Tallon, Florian Ferreira, Julien Milli, Magali Loupias, Isaac Bernardino Dinis, Emiliano Diolaiti, Markus Feldt, Raphael Galicher, Caroline Kulcsár, Johan Mazoyer, Mamadou Ndiaye, Henri-François Raynaud, Charles Goulas, Eric Stadler, Isabelle Tallon-Bosc, Anthony Boccaletti, Gael Chauvin, Nicolas Galland, Miska Lelouarn, Markus Kasper, Jalo Nousiainen, Arthur Vigan, Eric thiebaut, Fabrice Vidal, axel Potier, Francois Wildi, Gaele Barbary
Items.Title: SAXO+, the second-stage adaptive optics for SPHERE: high contrast performance analysis
Items.Abstract: SAXO+ is an upgrade of the SPHERE extreme adaptive optics system, which will boost the current high-contrast performance for the detection and characterization of exoplanets and circumstellar disks, and will serve as a demonstrator for the future Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (PCS) of the European ELT. The main drivers of the SAXO+ upgrade are: 1) to increase the contrast closer to the optical axis at short separations ranging from 0.1 to 0.5 arcseconds; 2) to observe fainter and redder stars compared to those observed with SPHERE; 3) to decrease the impact of fast-evolving turbulence thanks to a faster AO loop and the use of predictive control algorithms. We present the performance analysis of SAXO+ for a selection of science cases and turbulence conditions, including several coronagraphs.

Items.Authors: Eric Stadler, Laura Schreiber, Emiliano Diolaiti, Olivier Boebion, Yan Caujolle, Fausto Cortecchia, Alain Delboulbé, Matteo Lombini, Yves Magnard, Youssef Mohamed, Sylvain Rochat, Alain Spang, François Wildi, Gérard Zins, Gaël Chauvin, Manal Chebbo, Anne Costille, Philippe Delorme, Adriano De Rosa, Kjetil Dohlen, Markus Feldt, Florian Ferreira, Eric Gendron, Raffaele Gratton, Markus Kasper, Maud Langlois, Miska Le Louarn, Magali Loupias, Giuseppe Malaguti, Didier Maurel, Johan Mazoyer, Julien Milli, Gianluca Morgante, David Mouillet, Mamadou N'Diaye, Patrick Rabou, Filomena Schiavone, Alessandro Tacchini, Michel Tallon, Luca Terenzi, Fabrice Vidal, Gaële Barbary, Anthony Boccaletti
Items.Title: SAXO+, the second-stage adaptive optics for SPHERE: opto-mechanical components design and validation
Items.Abstract: SAXO+ is the second-stage adaptive optics (AO) module upgrading SPHERE at the ESO VLT. Downstream of the SAXO extreme AO system, it adds a fast near-IR loop targeting 3 kHz, reducing residual aberrations around the coronagraph and serving as a ELT PCS pathfinder. Because SPHERE is already crowded, SAXO+ uses an ultra-compact opto-mechanical design that fits on the bench. Alignment with SPHERE is achieved via three custom motorized tip-tilt mirrors with nanometric piezo actuators, allowing remote and seasonal realignment, if needed. The module includes a near-IR pyramid WFS, dichroic wheel, apodiser exchanger, and a high-speed electrostatic MEMS deformable mirror. Optical beam modulation relies on a commercial device driven by a custom controller, validated on a dedicated test bench. SAXO+ is now under assembly and lab alignment, for on-sky operation at the beginning of 2028.

Items.Authors: David Steenari
Items.Title: Scalable space instrument electrical architectures based on ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture): from multi-instrument missions to large-scale telescopes
Items.Abstract: The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) is a collaborative initiative by the European Space Agency, large system integrators, and data handling equipment suppliers to provide a modular and scalable standard for data handling equipment for space applications. The aim of ADHA is to reduce NRE (Non-Recurring Engineering) in flight projects, by providing standard electronics units and modules form-factors, a standard electrical backplane, and a standard procurement and AIT flow -- which is in-line with ESA's objective of reducing spacecraft development time, and promoting faster adoption innovative technologies.    This paper outlines how standardised ADHA-based hardware can be used to realise end-to-end electronics and software designs for different space instrument topologies and classes, including multi-instrument planetary missions, up to large-scale complex deep-space telescopes. The paper also provides example designs, their parameters and performances.

Items.Authors: Uma Subash, Samir Paudel, Menelaos K. Poutous, Hanshin Lee
Items.Title: Scalar diffraction modeling and experimental verification of beam propagation through amplitude grating for Talbot modulation lithography
Items.Abstract: This work presents the numerical modeling of the Talbot effect under free-space propagation through an amplitude grating. The modeling will be applied towards the development of a custom UV lithographic instrument that can generate grating patterns up to 12×12 sq.in in size, using Talbot modulation lithography. The 3D intensity pattern (Talbot carpet) of a 1 μm period and 50% duty cycle grating at UV illumination was modeled with diffraction calculations using scalar and rigorous algorithms. The need for precise positioning of the resist coated substrate at the self images is eliminated by modulating the substrate across the Talbot carpet. The accumulated intensity of 18 Talbot planes after bidirectional modulation cycles determined the total exposure time. The modeling is experimentally verified on a 50 μm period amplitude grating initially using spatially coherent illumination at 635 nm and 405 nm wavelength and later using a prototype illumination of the lithographic instrument.

Items.Authors: Nicholas K. MacDonald, Richard Deno Stelter, Michael Gonzales, Christopher Ratliff, Will Deich, Dale Sandford, JT Landry
Items.Title: SCALES mechanisms: from design to deployment of linear, rotary, and restricted rotary cryo-mechanisms
Items.Abstract: SCALES (the Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy) is a thermal infrared, lenslet-based IFS (integral field spectrograph) designed to work at the diffraction limit of the Keck II telescope. In order to maximize observational flexibility and instrumental capabilities, the SCALES team designed, fabricated, tested and tuned a variety of cryo-mechanisms at pupil planes (PP), focal planes (FP), or intermediate planes (IP). Due to the nominal operating temperature of 80 K, each mechanism requires careful planning to keep differential CTE mismatches negligible. The mechanisms include an encoded rotary servo coldstop and double filter wheel stack (PP), a linear slide (FP), a rotary mask selector (PP), tip-tilt piezo mirror (IP), a semi-rotary shutter (FP) and mode selector (IP), a dispersion carousel (PP), and lastly a second double filter wheel stack (IP). We describe the design requirements for each and detail the assembly and testing for each of the mechanisms.

Items.Authors: Shin Toriumi, Mari Nishiyama, Keiichi Matsuzaki, Toshifumi Shimizu, Hideki Kato, Jun Matsumoto, Mizuho Uchiyama, Kota Miyoshi, Daiki Yamasaki, Hirohisa Hara, Yukio Katsukawa, Masahito Kubo, Ryohko Ishikawa, Takenori J. Okamoto, Shinsuke Imada, Satoshi Masuda, Kyoko Watanabe, Yusuke Iida, Ayumi Asai
Items.Title: Science operation, data handling, and ground support system of the SOLAR-C mission
Items.Abstract: SOLAR-C is an upcoming solar-observing mission led by Japan, with major contributions from the U.S. and Europe, designed to advance solar physics through high-sensitivity EUV spectroscopic observations. Its onboard telescope, EUVST, will capture EUV spectra across a wide temperature range (10^4 - 10^7 K) with high spatial and temporal resolution to investigate the mechanisms of atmospheric heating and flare eruptions, supported by the EUV irradiance monitor, SoSpIM. To ensure robust operations, SOLAR-C employs heritage from Hinode and other preceding missions, with introducing cloud-based planning tools, rapid-response observation strategies, and high-speed data handling systems. Telemetry will be downlinked globally, processed at ISAS/JAXA and Nagoya University, and promptly released to the public.

Items.Authors: Sergio Salata, Jeff Kuhn, Nicolas Lodieu, Ricardo Diego, Mikel Armendia, Jose Antonio González, Ismael Ruiz de Argandoña, Ye Zhou
Items.Title: S-ELF 3.5m telescope: manufacture of mechanical structure and integration of motion control system
Items.Abstract: The IAC’s Laboratory for Innovation in Opto-Mechanics (LIOM) is developing the 3.5 m Small-ELF (S-ELF) prototype as a testbed for the future 50 m ExoLife Finder (ELF), aimed at achieving unprecedented exoplanet imaging performance through Fizeau interferometry. AVS manufactured the telescope from a DiSL design, delivering a lightweight, high-stiffness mount. The system uses top-grade components, dual encoders, and direct-drive torque motors for smooth, accurate tracking. Tekniker implemented the Beckhoff-based real-time control system with cascade controllers and sensor fusion for enhanced pointing accuracy. Factory tests confirmed <1 arcsec repeatability and validated structural behaviour under thermal and load conditions. The telescope will arrive at IACTEC in early 2026 for further integration and commissioning. This paper aims at demonstrating the successful integration of a lightweight design to serve as a cost-effective foundation for innovative astronomical applications.

Items.Authors: Peter Cramer, Aabid Patel, Michael da Silva, David Debski
Items.Title: Self-calibrating multi-head optical angular encoder architecture for long-duration space and telescope mechanisms
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a self-calibrating angular encoder architecture based on the discrete orthogonality of sinusoidal functions. When N optical read heads are uniformly distributed around a single encoder disk, spatial averaging of their outputs suppresses all cyclic error modes except those whose harmonic order is an integer multiple of N. This filtering property, derived directly from Fourier theory, enables encoders that inherently reject disk eccentricity, tilt, and other low-order geometric errors. A reference head placed at an incommensurate angular offset allows in-situ calibration of the remaining high-order components, permitting autonomous recalibration without external equipment. The approach provides a compact, radiation-hard, and long-life solution ideally suited to precision instruments and robotic systems used in space missions. More broadly, the results show that symmetry and Fourier structure can be used to realize robust, self-calibrating measurement systems.

Items.Authors: Changxi Yang, Yulei Ding, Yifei Wang, Chengying Bao
Items.Title: Self-injection locking microcombs and Raman lasers in AlN microcavities
Items.Abstract: Optical frequency combs (OFCs) have revolutionized astronomical spectroscopy by addressing long-standing challenges in wavelength calibration and radial velocity (RV) measurement. We investigate nonlinear self-injection locking in Aluminum nitride (AlN) microcavities, which generates stimulated Raman lasers and microcombs.  This approach achieves Raman laser emission with output exceeding 10 mW and a fundamental line width below 70 Hz in the 1750 nm band. Stokes platicon microcombs state are observed.

Items.Authors: Jessica S. Li, Aiden Shaheen, Keri Hoadley, Greyson Davis, Fernando Cruz Aguirre
Items.Title: Simulation and experimental demonstration of a three-mirror reflective element polarizer
Items.Abstract: This work presents the design and initial validation of an optical benchtop proof-of-concept (PoC) reflective element polarizer (REP) for future far-ultraviolet (FUV) astrophysical instrumentation. Polarimetry provides unique diagnostics of dust alignment, magnetic fields, and potential biosignature-related scattering, yet traditional transmissive polarizers suffer from low throughput in the FUV. A 3-mirror REP configuration is evaluated through Zemax (ZOS-API) simulations to quantify polarization-dependent throughput as a function of wavelength, coating, and incidence angle. Complementary benchtop measurements at 405, 520, and 639 nm provide experimental verification of polarization behavior. This proof-of-concept establishes a pathway toward efficient reflective polarizers that could enable next-generation FUV instrumentation for studies of dust, star and planet formation, and UV-sensitive biosignatures. This work also provides a framework for understanding polarization systems.

Items.Authors: Carmen Naletto, Paola Zuppella, Alberto Messetti, Vincenzo Della Corte, Lorenzo Guido Fiocco, Riccardo Bardazzi, Mirco Zaccariotto, Vania Da Deppo
Items.Title: Simulation of the EnVisS camera polarizing filters
Items.Abstract: EnVisS is an all-sky camera designed for the Comet Interceptor mission, an ESA Fast class mission that aims to explore and encounter a Dynamically New Comet.  The camera will study the radiance and polarization properties of the comet coma in the visible spectrum and is composed mainly of an optical head, a Filter Strip Assembly (FSA) and a detector.    The CNR-IFN of Padua and Leonardo SpA are responsible for designing the FSA, which has been manufactured by Materion Corporation.  To evaluate the optical performance of this component in terms of transmission and contrast ratio, some tests have been carried out in the CNR-IFN facilities on Moxtek linear polarizers, composing the FSA. In parallel, a simulation of the same analysis has been performed by means of the COMSOL Multiphysics software, comparing the theoretical and experimental results.    In this paper the simulations are illustrated and the results reported and compared with the experimental results obtained from previous analyses.

Items.Authors: Riccardo Lilli, Andrea Bocchieri, Fabio D'Anca, Federico Fiorenzoli, Daniele Gottini, Matthias Mann, Emanuele Pace, Enzo Pascale, Paolo Picchi, Andrea Tozzi, Antonio Scippa, Simon Schuler, Dervis Vernani, Javier Perez Alvarez, Andrés Perez Garcia, Anna Brucalassi, Andrew Caldwell, Paul Eccleston, Paolo Chioetto, Ciro Del Vecchio, Vincenzo Davide Cardinale, Elisa Guerriero, Giuseppina Micela, Pasquale Bonfà, Daniele Brienza, Manuele Gangi, Angelo Olivieri, Giovanna Tinetti, Elisabetta Tommasi, Paola Zuppella
Items.Title: Single point diamond turning optimization for the Ariel M1 large off-axis parabolic aluminum mirror
Items.Abstract: The primary mirror of the ARIEL Space Mission is a large lightweight elliptical mirror with an off-axis parabolic surface, where tight tolerances on Surface Form Error (SFE) and roughness are required. Single-Point Diamond Turning (SPDT) followed by polishing was selected to obtain the optical surface. A successful SPDT execution is critical to limiting the need for extensive polishing, which may introduce mid-frequency errors if overused. Improving SPDT process is not solely a matter of precision machining, but a variety of aspects must be considered. The mirror fixturing system was redesigned to minimize deformations due to the cutting process, and a dedicated mounting strategy was implemented. Once repeatable mounting was verified, a toolpath compensation strategy was applied, based on off-machine measurements using CMM and interferometry. This procedure achieved a reduction of more than 50% in SFE compared to previous manufacturing attempts, with values below SPDT requirements.

Items.Authors: Ewan Allan, Yuk-Shan Cheng, Kamalesh Dadi, Jake M. Charsley, William Newman, Hanna Ostapenko, Pablo Castro-Marín, Richard A. McCracken, Derryck T. Reid
Items.Title: Single-laser-diode-pumped 15-GHz Ti:sapphire astrocomb
Items.Abstract: Astrocombs provide thousands of ultra-narrow, regularly spaced and drift free optical frequencies on a multi-GHz grid enabling the precision, accuracy and traceability required for exoplanet observations. Here, we present a compact astrocomb system using a single-diode-pumped 1 GHz Ti:sapphire laser generating a supercontinuum spanning from 600 nm to 900 nm by using a photonic-crystal fiber. The supercontinuum light is filtered by a Fabry-Pérot cavity to a 15 GHz mode spacing to produce an astrocomb spanning 730 nm to 880 nm.

Items.Authors: Matteo Mallia, Olivier Deschaume, Jacob Pember, Gert Raskin, Christian Schwab, Julien Storm, Bart Vandenbussche, Sibo Van Gool
Items.Title: Sol-Gel dip-coating of large optics: developments for the MARVEL cross disperser prism
Items.Abstract: A sol-gel dip-coating process was developed and optimized for anti-reflection treatment of a large F2 glass prism used as cross-disperser in MARVEL, a high-resolution echelle spectrometer. Due to the large prism size and mass (40 kg), thermally assisted dielectric coatings are impractical. In the sol-gel dip-coating process, the prism is immersed in a colloidal silica suspension and withdrawn at a controlled speed, forming a uniform coating layer with controlled porosity. Sol-gel suspension recipes from the literature were prepared and characterized on small glass samples. The refractive index of the coating is tuned by adjusting the coating porosity, and its thickness is controlled through the withdrawal speed. The final process includes a dedicated dip-coating lift system and the experimental verification of coating thickness and of the optical performance on the MARVEL prism.

Items.Authors: Federico Battaini, Mirko Colapietro, Pietro Schipani, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Simone Di Filippo, Davide Ricci, Paolo D'Avanzo, Ricardo Zanmar Sanchez, Matteo Munari, Matteo Aliverti, Riccardo Claudi, Sergio Campana, Jani Achrén, José Antonio Araiza-Durán, Iair Arcavi, Laura Asquini, Andrea Baruffolo, Sagi Ben-Ami, Alex Bichkovsky, Federico Biondi, Anna Brucalassi, Lorenzo Cabona, Giulio Capasso, Enrico Cappellaro, Rosario Cosentino, Francesco D'Alessio, Sergio D'Orsi, Massimo Della Valle, Rosario Di Benedetto, Avishay Gal-Yam, matteo Genoni, Marcos Hernandez Díaz, Ofir Hershko, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Marco Landoni, Luigi Lessio, Gianluca Li Causi, Laurent Marty, Seppo Mattila, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio Pariani, Giuliano Pignata, Michael Rappaport, Marco Riva, Adam Rubin, Bernardo Salasnich, Slvatore Savarese, Salvatore Scuderi, Maximilian Stritzinger, Stephen Smartt, Hector Pérez Ventura, Fabrizio Vitali, David Young
Items.Title: SOXS at NTT: ADC journey from integration to on-sky performance
Items.Abstract: The Son Of X-Shooter (SOXS) is the specialized spectroscopy-follow-up facility for transient events with a flexible scheduler at the ESO NTT. The instrument spans from 350nm up to 2000nm with an average of R∼4500 for a 1” slit. The visible arm (350-800nm), includes an Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (ADC) composed of two powered quadruplets. In a previous work we presented the alignment and integration strategy and results. The ADC is now working at the telescope and we can summarize its peculiarity, the optical performance as measured in the laboratory and the on-sky verification after the telescope-AIV in 2025.

Items.Authors: Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Federico Battaini, Mirko Colapietro, Simone Di Filippo, Matteo Aliverti, Davide Ricci, Paolo D'Avanzo, Pietro Schipani, Sergio Campana, David Young, Marco Landoni, Matteo Munari, Stephen Smartt, Matteo Genoni, Riccardo Claudi, Fabrizio Vitali, Salvatore Scuderi, Salvatore Savarese, Sergio D'Orsi, Rosario Cosentino, Frédéric Dérie, Markus Schoeller, Armin Silber, Ivo Saviane, Andrea Modigliani, Emanuela Pompei, Derek Ives, Matteo Accardo, Géza Csörnyei, Luca Pasquini, Antonio Miccichè, Gaetano Nicotra, Eugenio Martinetti, Silvio Di Rosa, Marco Dima, Simone Doniselli, Lorenzo Cabona, Ricardo Zanmar Sanchez, Bernardo Salasnich, Adam Rubin, Marco Riva, Michael Rappaport, Giuliano Pignata, Luigi Lessio, Laurent Marty, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Ofir Hershko, Francesco D'Alessio, Giulio Capasso, Anna Brucalassi, Alex Bichkovsky, Sagi Ben-Ami, Andrea Baruffolo, José A. Araiza-Durán, Maximilian Stritzinger, Seppo Mattila, Avishay Gal-Yam, Iair Arcavi, Massimo Della Valle, Enrico Cappellaro
Items.Title: SOXS at the NTT: installation and commissioning
Items.Abstract: The Son Of X-Shooter (SOXS) has been installed at ESO’s New Technology Telescope. Simultaneous spectroscopic observations covering the 0.35–2.0 μm wavelength range, with a spectral resolution of 4500 for a 1″ slit, targeting time-domain and transient phenomena, are expected to begin shortly after completion of nighttime commissioning. Over the past two years, SOXS has achieved major milestones, including successful AIV in Italy and PAE. The instrument was shipped to Chile in 31 crates and arrived at La Silla Observatory on January 31, 2025. Reassembly, alignment, and full functional verification were completed at the NTT. On-site activities included instrument–telescope interfacing, technical nighttime verification of subsystems and system performance, and validation of control software and data-reduction pipelines using on-sky data. At the time of writing, commissioning is ongoing, with results confirming compliance with spectral resolution requirements.

Items.Authors: John Wallis, Elrina Hartman, Joshua Collier, David Gozzard
Items.Title: Spatial mode demultiplexing for high-resolution astronomical imaging
Items.Abstract: Quantum imaging has achieved impressive results in fields such as microscopy and lithography where the target object can be probed by engineered light sources such as entangled sources. However, in astronomy, we cannot influence the target objects and must make maximum use of the information available in the arriving photons.     We present results of laboratory experiments advancing the spatial mode demultiplexing (SPADE) quantum imaging technique for astronomy. We show that SPADE is able to simultaneously recover accurate separation and relative brightness information of artificial binary star systems well below the diffraction limit. We achieved a best performance of accurate determination of the separation and relative brightness of our two stars two orders of magnitude below the diffraction limit.

Items.Authors: Richard Vanfleet, Devin Lewis, Joshua Hancock, Javier G. Del Hoyo, David Allred, Mateo F. Batkis, Luis V. Rodriguez de Marcos, Manuel A. Quijada
Items.Title: Stability of astrophysically important metal-fluoride coatings under electron dosing
Items.Abstract: We investigated the stability of metal-fluoride coatings for aluminum mirrors under electron beam conditions to predict their lifetime in deep space conditions. The mirrors were exposed to electron radiation by placing them under the beam of a scanning electron microscope (SEM) under various electron energies and currents.   For LiF, visible roughening was apparent, and loss of LiF from the surface was detected by energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). Loss of fluorine was the highest for electron energies ranging from 350-500 eV with damage decreasing with lower or higher energies.   MgF2 samples underwent oxygen plasma treatment to remove surface carbon contamination and were then exposed to similar conditions and experiments as the LiF study. In contrast to LiF coatings, plasma-treated MgF2 samples saw no loss of Mg or F in EDX and no visual roughening during SEM imaging. MgF2 samples that were contaminated with carbon did show loss of F during e-beam exposure.

Items.Authors: Stephen E. Levine, Timothy Ellsworth-Bowers
Items.Title: Status of the 4.3-meter Lowell Discovery Telescope (LDT): new instruments, same notable performance
Items.Abstract: The Lowell Discovery Telescope (LDT) is a 4.3-m telescope designed and constructed for optical and near infrared astronomical observation [1,2]. This report looks at the evolution over time of the performance of the facility. We are planning for the addition of three new instruments and new facility monitoring systems.

Items.Authors: Jaren N. Ashcraft, Ramya Anche, Ewan S. Douglas, Jessica Gersh-Range, Kyle van Gorkom, Roser Juanola-Parramon, Saraswathi Kalyani, Maxwell A. Millar-Blanchaer, A .J. Riggs, Breann Sitarski
Items.Title: Strategies for maximizing throughput in high-contrast ultraviolet apodized pupil lyot coronagraphs
Items.Abstract: NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory aims to detect and characterize ~25 potential habitable exoplanets to constrain the presence of life in the universe. We characterize planets in the UV to search for ozone, because it helps us to constrain the age of habitable worlds. Throughput is a primary concern in the UV because of the low transmission per-optic. However, the smaller diffraction limit in the UV means that a habitable exoplanet is farther from the core of the coronagraph’s point-spread function. We conduct a design survey using open-source tools that utilize GPU-accelerated algorithmic differentiation to optimize the coronagraph masks. We explore relaxed inner working angles for a series of amplitude and phase-apodized lyot coronagraphs to isolate strategies for maximizing core throughput in a UV Coronagraph for HWO. We find that relaxing the IWA constraint in the UV can double a coronagraph's core throughput, and decrease a coronagraph’s sensitivity to low-order aberrations.

Items.Authors: Seri Yeon, Jihun Kim, Yunjong Kim, Tom Davies, Yeonsik Kim, Il Kweon Moon, Dohoon Kim, Hyuksun Kwon, Kyohoon Ahn, GyeongGon Bahk, Woowon Byun, Seunghyuk Chang, Daewook Kim, Seonwoo Kim, Gayoung Lee, Jongwan Ko
Items.Title: Stray light analysis of the K-DRIFT G1 telescope using measured bidirectional scattering distribution function
Items.Abstract: The KASI Deep Rolling Imaging Fast Telescope (K-DRIFT) Generation 1 (G1) is an off-axis freeform three-mirror telescope for observing low-surface-brightness (LSB) structures. Since LSB imaging demands high contrast, stray light must be characterized and controlled. In this study, we performed a stray light analysis of the K-DRIFT G1 using measured optical coating and bidirectional scattering distribution function (BSDF) data. We first analyzed ghost images to identify the reflecting surfaces and paths, then evaluated the performance degradation due to stray light using point source transmittance (PST) simulation, which revealed the dominant incidence angles and their ray paths. Comparison with previous analyses based on idealized inputs showed that the measured inputs yield higher stray light levels and identified the surfaces most sensitive to measured data, highlighting the importance of measured inputs for stray light analysis.

Items.Authors: Zhu Yuji, Yonghe Chen, Chuanxin Wei
Items.Title: Stray light suppression design for the ET Transit Telescope
Items.Abstract: To ensure that The Earth 2.0 (ET) transit telescopes achieves the ultra-high-precision photometric capability required for detecting exoplanets, the internal stray light background noise must be suppressed to an extremely low level. This paper aims to complete an efficient stray light suppression design through systematic simulation analysis and verification. Using TracePro optical analysis software, an accurate model of the transit telescope was constructed, incorporating all optical and mechanical components and surface properties (such as the Bidirectional Scattering Distribution Function (BSDF) of black paint coatings). Stray light simulation analysis was conducted using the forward ray-tracing method to identify critical stray light paths. Furthermore, the Point Source Transmittance (PST) values at different off-axis angles of the light source were calculated. The results indicate that the combined effect of multi-stage baffles and highly absorptive coatings significantly suppress

Items.Authors: Junlin Ma, Changhua Liu, Zhiyi Wang, Yuyan Cao, Peng Guo, Li Huo
Items.Title: Structural design and analysis of large target plane 2x2 spliced detector for astronomical observation
Items.Abstract: This project develops a 2.5-meter wide-field astronomical telescope for near-Earth asteroid detection, space-debris surveillance, and high-cadence time-domain sky surveys. It achieves 21-mag sensitivity with a field of view over 3 degrees in the 0.42–0.8 μm band, enabling rapid, wide-area sky monitoring. It provides high-speed tracking with azimuth and elevation velocities of 15°/s and 6°/s while maintaining fine tracking precision at the 10⁻⁴–10⁻² °/s level. Rapid angular-acceleration capability ensures accurate tracking of fast-moving targets.The telescope integrates advanced optical design, precision opto-mechanics, a lightweight yet rigid structure, and a robust servo-control platform, ensuring stable imaging and reliable long-term operation. It serves as a versatile facility for planetary-defense warning, space-situational awareness, transient detection, and time-domain astrophysics.

Items.Authors: Shuli Song, Weili Zhou, Massinissa Hadjara
Items.Title: Study on global ionospheric TEC modeling and scintillation monitoring based on GNSS
Items.Abstract: The terrestrial ionosphere influences electromagnetic waves, impacting navigation signals, space vehicles, and infrastructure. Strong disturbances cause interference, and the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) provides crucial ionospheric data for modeling and research. This study proposes a global TEC modeling method that fuses GNSS and virtual observations with automatic bias calibration, improving reliability in large station gaps. Using slant TEC (STEC) and VOSs, the model reduces the RMSE of estimated GIMs by up to 53%, with performance comparable to IGS products. The method has been applied to China's deep space missions. Additionally, a real-time global TEC model is updated hourly, reducing time delay from 1-2 days to 1-2 hours. The study also explores ionospheric scintillation detection and methods to mitigate its impact on kinematic PPP.

Items.Authors: Yong‘an Liu, Yalong Zhang, Zhe Liu, Yifan Lu, Lizhi Sheng
Items.Title: Study on the performance of photon-counting imaging detector for space-based ultraviolet detection
Items.Abstract: A photon-counting imaging detector based on induction readout has been developed for space-based observations of ultraviolet radiation in the ionosphere. By employing image charge technology, this detector achieves physical isolation between the high-voltage section and the electronic readout circuitry, thereby significantly enhancing the operational reliability of the detector. The detector utilizes a reflective CsI photocathode with an effective area of 40 mm in diameter. The performance of the detector was tested using an ultraviolet detector imaging evaluation system. The results show that the dark count rate is below 10 counts·s⁻¹, spatial resolution better than 90 μm, and detection efficiency greater than 15% at 121 nm. Having been developed for space applications, this detector is now operational and will remain instrumental in space-based ultraviolet observation missions over the next several years.

Items.Authors: Hirofumi Okita, Yutaka Hayano, Jun Omiya, Hironori Tsutsui, Yoshinori Kumura, Koichi Sawatari
Items.Title: Subaru Telescope’s reflectivity measurements: 8.5-years measurements and results
Items.Abstract: Subaru Telescope has developed the Subaru Portable Spectrophotometer (SPS) and has been continuously in-situ measuring the reflectivity of the primary mirror and other mirrors on the telescope since October 2017, and it becomes ~8.5 years in July 2026. To understand reflectivity degradation of mirrors, we developed reflectivity models for aluminum and silver mirrors. Over these 8.5 years, the telescope has also experienced at least 5 times of major volcanic events and 4 times of close encounters with hurricanes and tropical storms. We found that the impact of volcanic events was limited, while high-humidity events caused significant degradation in reflectivity. We also applied reflectivity measurement to study wash cleaning and mirror damage evaluation. The continuous reflectivity measurements in the 8.5 years has been contributed to deciding the maintenance schedule, including the renovations of the coating chamber control and the air conditioning system of the enclosure.

Items.Authors: Elena Tonucci, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Warren B. Foster, Jared R. Males, Olivier Guyon, Laird M. Close, Kyle Van Gorkom, Alexander D. Hedglen, Parker T. Johnson, Maggie Y. Kautz, Jay K. Kueny, Rico Landman, Jialin Li, Joshua Liberman, Joseph D. Long, Miles Lucas, Jennifer Lumbres, Matthijs Mars, Eden A. McEwen, Avalon McLeod, Tiffany Nguyen, Logan A. Pearce, María Eugenia Redondo González, Lauren Schatz, Katie Twitchell
Items.Title: Sub-diffraction-limited coronagraphic imaging with nano-printed PIAACMC phase masks
Items.Abstract: The extreme contrast and small separations needed to image Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones cannot be reached with current technology. The Phase-Induced Amplitude Apodization Complex Mask Coronagraph (PIAACMC) is a promising device to reach this goal. With its aspheric lenses to losslessly apodize the entrance pupil and a phase-shifting focal plane mask for starlight suppression, it allows us to achieve high throughput and small inner-working angle (IWA). The masks are manufactured in-house at Leiden University with Nanoscribe, a nano-3D-printer that uses two-photon polymerization achieving submicron precision in height.  We present the first on-sky performance results of the PIAACMC at visible wavelengths and the detection of faint companions at separations 0.8-5λ/D (~23-145mas) with MagAO-X, the extreme adaptive optics instrument for the 6.5m Magellan Clay telescope at Las Campanas Observatory. This demonstrates the PIAACMC’s capability to observe at the diffraction limit.

Items.Authors: Lucas Marquis, Fabio Bosin, Liurong Lin, Ruben Tandon, Yves Emery, Jonas G. Kühn
Items.Title: Sub-nanometer spatio-temporal phase metrology of classical LCOS SLMs: calibration efforts towards adaptive coronagraphy
Items.Abstract: Spatial Light Modulators (SLMs) are numerically programmable optical components that modulate the phase of light. We present digital holographic microscope (DHM) metrology results for the calibration of two classical liquid-crystal on-silicon (LCOS) VIS-633 nm SLMs: Meadowlark P1920 and Holoeye ERIS-NIR-153. For both devices, we assessed the phase response in real-time, with sub-nanometer precision along the optical axis, and micrometric lateral resolution. The phase response includes the command-to-phase relation (look-up tables) and the pixels' impulse response. We also characterized the static (wavefront error) and temporal behavior across short timescales to derive stability. We introduce our DHM and the SLM calibration procedures, performance metrics and the simulated practical impact on coronagraphic performance. Particular emphasis is placed on the implications for the SLM-equipped PLACID direct-imaging instrument, which is currently being commissioned on the 4-m DAG telescope.

Items.Authors: Marianna Michelagnoli, Mauro Focardi, Pierpaolo Merola, Fredrik Leffe Johansson, Gregoire Deprez, Francois Gutierrez, Marina Vela Nuñez, Vladimiro Noce, Simone Chiarucci, Elisabetta Giani, Gianluca Marotta
Items.Title: Surface charging analyses of the Ariel spacecraft in transient plasma environments around L2
Items.Abstract: This work presents the results of recent simulations in the relevant plasma environments that the Ariel (Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large-survey) spacecraft will encounter during its operational orbit around L2, including transients between different plasma regimes, where not negligible surface charging phenomenon is expected to occur. The objective of this study is to analyse the effects of these transient conditions to understand how the spacecraft’s surface charges will redistribute.

Items.Authors: Silvio Di Rosa, Marco Dima, Tania Sofia Gomes Machado, Demetrio Magrin, Davide Greggio, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Roberto Ragazzoni, Luigi Lessio, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Jacopo Farinato, Simone Zaggia
Items.Title: Surface quality improvement of 3D printed lenses for astronomical use
Items.Abstract: The first steps of an ongoing investigation regarding the manufacturing of optical-quality lenses using PolyJet 3D-printing technologies is presented. The study aims to identify possible post-processing routes in order to increase the surface quality of 3D printed optical components, currently one of the key challenges in producing lenses with additive manufacturing.

Items.Authors: Letizia Casara, Matteo Cantoresi, Francesco Berrilli, Luca Giovannelli, Valentina Penza, Dario Del Moro, Serena Criscuoli
Items.Title: Synthetic UV solar observations for space weather CubeSats
Items.Abstract: We present a simulation tool that supports the design and performance assessment of UV detectors for satellite solar imagers. It generates realistic synthetic focal-plane images by combining radiative-transfer models with spatial information from segmented solar observations. As a test case, we simulate the 279–281 nm band around the Mg II line, assigning spectral radiance to plages, network, and quiet Sun via a semiempirical model (SRPM). The radiance map is then processed through a complete instrument chain, including filter bandpass, PSF, detector response, and noise, producing end-to-end mock observations. This approach is crucial for future UV imagers targeting the lower chromosphere, providing data to optimize instrument parameters, evaluate signal-to-noise and contrast, and validate mission requirements related to solar irradiance variability and space-weather studies.

Items.Authors: John A. Kypriotakis, Siddharth Maharana, Abhay Kohok, Neetika Keserwani, Pravin Khodade, Chaitanya Rajarshi, Bhushan Joshi, Anamparambu N. Ramaprakash, Namita Uppal, Ramya Anche, Dmitry Blinov, Hans Kristian Eriksen, Myrto Falalaki, Tuhin Ghosh, Eirik Gjerløw, Brandon Hensley, Chryssi Koukouraki, Yannis Liodakis, Nidhi Mehandiratta, Johanna Mueller, Georgia Panopoulou, Vasiliki Pavlidou, Timothy Pearson, Stephen Potter, Raphael Skalidis, Anthony Readhead, Konstantinos Tassis, Ingunn Wehus
Items.Title: Systems design, assembly and integration of WALOP-North optical polarimeter
Items.Abstract: WALOP-North (Wide-Area Linear Optical Polarimeter), developed as part of the PASIPHAE survey, will be deployed on the 1.3 m Skinakas Observatory telescope in Crete, Greece to carry out a large optical polarization survey covering thousands of square degrees. The instrument is designed to deliver imaging polarimetry over a 30′×30′ field in the SDSS-r filter with polarimetric accuracy of 0.1%. Together with WALOP-South, WALOPs will be the first wide-field survey capacity polarimeters in optical wavelengths. Using a four-channel, one-shot polarimetry design with no moving parts and a large-format CCDs, WALOP-North is optimized for high accuracy polarimetry and stability, throughput, and survey efficiency, and is currently being integrated and prepared for commissioning. We will present its design, lab assembly, integration, and characterization.

Items.Authors: Hemanth Pruthvi, Hans-Peter Doerr, Michael Sigwarth, Markus Roth
Items.Title: TauSoL imaging spectropolarimeter for synoptic solar observations
Items.Abstract: Tautenburg Solar Laboratory (TauSoL) is a pathfinder for a future network of solar monitoring telescopes, namely Solar Physics Research Integrated Network Group (SPRING). For this ground-based network, a principal instrument is high-cadence multi-line spectropolarimeter. The instrument would produce full-disk Dopplergrams and magnetograms of the Sun corresponding to several heights in the solar atmosphere, enabling continuous observations of solar activity as well as helioseismology.   At TauSoL, we are developing a prototype using airgap Fabry-Pérot interferometer as a narrow passband tunable filter. In the first phase, the instrument is commissioned to operate in spectroscopy mode with Fe I 630.25 nm spectral line to produce line-of-sight velocity maps corresponding to the solar photosphere.

Items.Authors: Antonio Scippa, Daniele Gottini, Riccardo Lilli, Andrea Tozzi, Paolo Picchi, Luca Carbonaro, Ciro Del Vecchio, Anna Brucalassi, Javier Perez-Alvarez, Andres Perez-Garcia, Alejandro Fernandez-Soler, Paolo Chioetto, Paola Zuppella, Fabio D'Anca, Vincenzo Cardinale, Luisa Sciortino, Elisa Guerriero, Giuseppina Micela, Giampaolo Preti, Emanuele Pace, Pasquale Bonfà, Daniele Brienza, Manuele Gangi, Elisabetta Tommasi, Angelo Olivieri, Andrea Bocchieri, Andrew Caldwell, Paul Eccleston, Giovanna Tinetti
Items.Title: TCC evaluation of complex metallic junctions: the Ariel case
Items.Abstract: This documents describe the hybrid numerical/experimental study used to evaluate the Thermal Contact Conductance (TCC) of mechanical interfaces within the Ariel mission’s telescope assembly. To address initial overestimation of thermal gradients, Finite Element simulations were combined with experimental testing on specialised mock-ups of the Primary Mirror and Optical Bench. The methodology utilized static structural analysis to map contact pressure, which was then translated into thermal conductance values through semi-empirical models and validated through steady-state temperature measurements in a vacuum chamber. Strategic sensor placement and rigorous calibration protocols were implemented to manage uncertainties related to effective bolt preloads and secondary heat paths. Ultimately, the findings provided a correlated data-set designed to refine structural thermal-optical performance (STOP) models and optimise the mechanical integration of space-based optical instrument.

Items.Authors: Anthony Santini, David Morris, Andres Parraguez Carcamo, Alexandra Tritschler
Items.Title: Techniques for analyzing the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope Engineering Data Store
Items.Abstract: The Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope implements a constant, high cadence monitoring of many key observational metrics including summit weather, instrument status, wavefront status, telescope position, optical path status and calibration script results. This data is stored in the Engineering Data Store database (EDS) and can be used as reference when determining the exact status of the observatory at any arbitrary time. The cumulation of this data over the last five years has generated a substantial archive of data, the processing of which allows for the construction of historical trends and statistical analysis of observational methods. These analyses are used to determine and quantify issues and analyze observing conditions which enables various improvements to operational efficiency. The process of implementing this from the creation of the software tools to query from the EDS to the processing and interpretation will be described in this paper.

Items.Authors: Andrea Bianco, Marco Riva, Letizia Caito, Enrico Giro, Sofia Randich, Emma Fernández-Alvar, Oscar Gonzalez, Sergio G. Sousa, Laura Magrini
Items.Title: Technologies challenges and developments for HRMOS at the VLT
Items.Abstract: HRMOS (https://www.hrmos.eu/) is a new instrument we plan to propose for the ESO VLT. HRMOS target resolving power is 80000 in three spectral windows with a total range of 140nm in the visible. It will have Multiplexing capabilities in the range of 40 to 80 and will be characterized by a radial velocity precision of 10m/s. Such an ambitious instrument presents some technological challenges to be addressed that will turn into important “enabling” technological activities. These activities will be crucial for the instrument itself, but they align with known challenges in ELT instrumentation. Examples of such technologies are: i) Large size (400 mm in diameter) and high dispersion diffraction gratings; ii) optical fibers; iii) CMOS instead of CCD detectors.  This paper will highlight these technological developments showing the impact on HRMOS and future optical instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Andreas Quirrenbach, CARMENES Consoritum
Items.Title: Ten years of exoplanet discoveries and stellar astrophysics with CARMENES
Items.Abstract: The CARMENES instrument at the 3.5m telescope on Calar Alto, which consists of two cross-dispersed echelle spectrographs covering the wavelength range from 0.5 to 1.7 microns, entered scientific operations on Jan 1st, 2016. Since then, it has been used for a radial-velocity (RV) survey of 362 M dwarf stars, for RV follow-up of planet transit candidates from TESS, for transmission spectroscopy of transiting planets, and a few smaller programs. A total of 85 planets have been discovered or confirmed with CARMENES, some of them with masses as low as 1 Earth mass. A statistical analysis shows that such planets are abundant for ultra-low mass stars. The combination of the CARMENES and TESS data shows that the composition of terrestrial planets of M dwarfs is similar to that of the Earth. The Helium line at 1.083 microns is a powerful diagnostic of evaporation from strongly irradiated giant planets. We will discuss these findings along with our results on the properties of low-mass stars.

Items.Authors: Jonathan Wei, Oliver Pineda Suárez, Malak Galal, Maxime Rombach, Sébastien Pernecker, Stefane Caseiro, Corentin Magnenat, Florian Boeckle, Jean-Paul Kneib
Items.Title: Testing of a 15-positioner module based on the MPS design for stage-5 telescopes
Items.Abstract: Assessing the performance metrics of theta-phi micro-robotic positioners is a key step toward understanding their operational behavior and ensuring that they meet the specifications of Stage-5 astronomical facilities, including the Chinese MUST, the American Spec-S5, and the European WST. A detailed examination of these metrics guides improvements in design and manufacturing. In this work, carried out in collaboration with Micro Precision Systems (MPS) in Switzerland, we present the results of positioning performance and angular tilt characterization conducted on a 6.2-mm-pitch robotic positioner module developed for high-density fiber placement in next-generation spectroscopic instruments. The measured metrics, including positioning repeatability, datum repeatability, backlash, non-linearity, and angular tilt, are compared directly with the nominal performance targets defined for Stage-5 telescope systems.

Items.Authors: Kersten Mumme, Freerk Schütt, Viljon Sekseni, Martin Backer, Sabine Tiedeken, Philipp Huke
Items.Title: Testing the coupling efficiency distribution of fibers with improved optical interfaces
Items.Abstract: Effective free space to fiber coupling requires high spatial accuracy, which for a small number of such interfaces is manageable,   but for larger numbers results in a statistical misalignment between the incoupling optics and the fiber.   Alterations to the fiber might allow for improvement in the coupling efficiency at larger inaccuracies.   To verify this, we propose an automated measurement setup for testing the coupling efficiency under longitudinal, lateral and rotational misalignments.  Possible alterations to the fibers include ball lenses, ball lenses made from no core fibers and ball lenses added to a tapered no core fiber.  We hope, that by adding these alterations to the fiber, we can guarantee a higher coupling efficiency in a system with many   free space to fiber interfaces.

Items.Authors: G. Lombardi, N. Almalik, O. Cuevas Ahumada, G. Fildes, T. Y. Alrefay
Items.Title: The AlUla Manara Observatory Complex: site characterization with integrated turbulence, meteorology, and aerosol assessment from a 24-hour operating Astronomical Site Monitor
Items.Abstract: The AlUla Manara Observatory project envisions a new astronomical facility in north-western Saudi Arabia, supported by a site-testing program that combines reanalysis climatology and continuous ground measurements. We report results from the Astronomical Site Monitor (ASM), operating since April 2025 as the region's first autonomous site-monitoring system. The ASM includes a 24hSHIMM turbulence profiler, a 4-level meteorological tower, a dust sensor, and an RPG-HATPRO radiometer. SHIMM data shows stable daytime turbulence and limited nocturnal variability. Meteorological data show moderate thermal gradients and mild winds, while dust is the main constraint. The dust assessment defines enclosure requirements, optical-surface active and passive protection policies, operational risk criteria and mitigation strategies required in the design and operation of the observatory. The dataset defines the first astroclimatological envelope for Manara and supports telescope and observatory design.

Items.Authors: Aafaque R. Khan, Willam T. Verts, Daniel Turong, Harrison Bradley, Ipek Kerkesser, Elijah Garcia, Hannah Tanquary, Haeun Chung, Carlos Vargas, Erika Hamden, Heejoo Choi, Daewook Kim, Brock A. Parker
Items.Title: The Aspera SmallSat mission: pre-flight performance and characterization of FUV spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Aspera is a NASA SmallSat mission designed to map faint O VI 103.2 nm emission from warm–hot diffuse gas in nearby galaxy halos. The payload includes two identical FUV Rowland-circle long-slit spectrographs sharing an MCP detector, enabling the first spatially resolved far-UV emission maps of this gas phase. We present the pre-flight optical and detector characterization—throughput, spectral calibration, spatial and spectral PSF, and detector background—performed before and after environmental testing in a dedicated FUV calibration setup in a class 1000 cleanroom. The system uses a VUV monochromator and an Ar+H hollow-cathode lamp producing the H Ly-β and Ar I lines for alignment and calibration. A pickoff mirror directs part of the beam to an EM MCP detector calibrated to a NIST-traceable VUV photodiode, enabling absolute flux comparison. These measurements, combined with component characterization, form the as-built performance model for Aspera’s 2026 launch.

Items.Authors: Jeremy J. Drake, Paul A. Scowen, Robert A. Woodruff, Gayley G. Gayley, Richard Ignace, Christiana Erba, Roberto Casini, Kathleen M. Coderre, Megan A. DeMott, Kristin D. Doney, Samantha F. Edgington, Matthew W. Gilbertson
Items.Title: The design and engineering of the Polstar Far Ultraviolet Spectropolarimetry mission
Items.Abstract: Polstar is a Small Explorer mission concept for a far-ultraviolet high-resolution spectropolarimeter operating in the 115-280nm range. Polstar provides a new observational window for understanding the physics of high-mass stars and how rotation affects their evolution and their routes to forming compact object remnants. It captures all four Stokes parameters (IQUV) at a spectral resolution of 20,000, equivalent to a velocity resolution of 15 km/s. Polarization sensitivity reaches as low as 0.03%, providing powerful new insights into stellar oblateness and rotation, circumstellar disks, and emission geometry. Polstar also has great capacity for a vigorous and scientifically diverse Guest Observer program in an extended mission phase. Here, we present the latest developments in the design and engineering of the Polstar instrument and spacecraft.
